title: Module Constants and Nesting
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of module constants and nesting in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply module constants and nesting in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to constant lookup rules and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Module Constants and Nesting through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding module constants and nesting helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Module Constants and Nesting helps you reason about namespaced constants. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Namespaced constants. Then connect it to Fully qualified constant names. The remaining syllabus points—Constant lookup rules—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Module Constants and Nesting
content_blocks.code:
module Timestamped
  def timestamp_label
    "created at: #{Time.now.year}"
  end
end
class Report
  include Timestamped
end
puts Report.new.timestamp_label

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports module constants and nesting. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap

Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
